record.original_question: Is every search for three-step or higher-step homogeneous geodesics reducible to the study of two-step homogeneous geodesics, so that products of three or more exponential factors introduce no essentially new phenomenon beyond the two-step case?

evidence.quote: Concerning generalizations of the g.o. propery, we have introduced the concept of a two-step homogeneous geodesic and two-step g.o. space. We conjecture that a search for three-step (or more) homogeneous geodesics reduces to two-step homogeneous geodesics.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M=G/K,g)$ be a Riemannian homogeneous space, where $G$ is a connected Lie group acting transitively by isometries on $M$ and $K$ is the isotropy subgroup at the origin $o\in M$. Let $\mathfrak{g}=\mathrm{Lie}(G)$ and fix a reductive decomposition $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{k}\oplus\mathfrak{m}$ with $\mathrm{Ad}(K)\mathfrak{m}\subset\mathfrak{m}$, and identify $\mathfrak{m}\cong T_oM$.

For an integer $k\geq 1$, a smooth curve $\gamma:\mathbb{R}\to M$ is called a $k$-step homogeneous geodesic if $\gamma$ is a geodesic of $(M,g)$ and there exist $X_1,\dots,X_k\in\mathfrak{g}$ such that
$$\gamma(t)=\pi\bigl(\exp(tX_1)\exp(tX_2)\cdots\exp(tX_k)\bigr)\qquad \text{for all }t\in\mathbb{R},$$
where $\pi:G\to G/K$ is the natural projection. The case $k=1$ recovers the usual notion of a homogeneous geodesic (orbit of a one-parameter subgroup), and $k=2$ is the notion of a two-step homogeneous geodesic.

Prove or disprove the following statement: for every Riemannian homogeneous space $(G/K,g)$ and every integer $k\geq 3$, the existence and structure of $k$-step homogeneous geodesics reduces to the two-step case. More precisely, every geodesic of $(G/K,g)$ that admits a representation as a $k$-step homogeneous geodesic for some $k\geq 3$ also admits a representation as a two-step homogeneous geodesic, so that products of three or more exponential factors yield no essentially new geodesics beyond those obtained with two factors.
artifact.category_tag: homogeneous geodesics on Riemannian homogeneous spaces
artifact.status_search_result: The notion of two-step homogeneous geodesics and two-step g.o. spaces has been developed in subsequent works (e.g., a 2016 Taiwanese J. Math. paper and a 2021 arXiv preprint on Finsler analogs), but no source located states a proof or disproof of the conjectural reduction of $k$-step ($k\geq 3$) homogeneous geodesics to the two-step case. The status appears to remain a conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Two-step Homogeneous Geodesics in Homogeneous Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces and studies two-step homogeneous geodesics γ(t)=π(exp(tX)exp(tY)) on Riemannian homogeneous spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Two-step homogeneous geodesics are an active concept; the source studies the two-step case without resolving the higher-step reduction question.

status_evidence.title: Two-step homogeneous geodesics in some homogeneous Finsler manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Defines two-step homogeneous g.o. spaces in the Finsler setting and gives examples (Wallach spaces, flag manifolds, k-symmetric spaces).
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent works extend the two-step concept but do not establish reduction of three-or-more-step geodesics to two-step geodesics.
